Class ListIteratorAdapterTest

java.lang.Object
myTest.ListIteratorAdapterTest
public class ListIteratorAdapterTest extends Object
Test suite for the ListIteratorAdapter class.

This test suite validates the functionality of the ListIteratorAdapter class, which implements the HListIterator interface to provide bidirectional iteration over elements of a VectorAdapter or SubListAdapter. The tests cover various scenarios including forward and backward traversal, element modification, insertion, removal, and edge cases.

Test Case Design

The test cases are designed to validate the behavior of ListIteratorAdapter against the specifications of Java 1.4.2 ListIterator interface. The test design includes categories for basic functionality, edge cases, error conditions, and sublist-specific behavior.

Categories:

  • Basic bidirectional iteration tests
  • Index position tracking tests
  • Element modification tests (set, add, remove)
  • Empty collection tests
  • Null element handling tests
  • SubList iterator tests
  • Exception handling tests
  • ListIterator with specific starting index tests

    • testNextIndexProperOrder

      public void testNextIndexProperOrder()
      Test method to verify that nextIndex() returns the correct index when iterating through the list in forward order.

      Summary:

      This test verifies that the nextIndex() method of a HListIterator correctly returns the index of the element that would be returned by a subsequent call to next() at every step during a full forward traversal of the list.

      Test Case Design:

      The test is designed to validate the fundamental contract of the nextIndex() method during normal iteration. It ensures that the reported index always correctly corresponds to the current position of the iterator and matches the index of the element in the underlying list.

      Test Description:

      The test iterates through the entire list using the iterator's hasNext() and next() methods. Before each call to next(), it checks that the value returned by nextIndex() is equal to the index of the element that is about to be returned. This element is also fetched directly from the underlying list using the get() method for comparison.

      Pre-Condition:

      - A VectorAdapter is initialized with elements: ["1", "2", "3", null, "5"]

      - A HListIterator is obtained from the vector

      Post-Condition:

      - The iterator has been traversed to the end of the list

      - All assertions have passed

      Expected Results:

      For every step of the iteration, the value returned by listIterator.nextIndex() must be equal to the index of the element returned by the subsequent listIterator.next() call, and this element must equal the element at that same index in the original vector (vector.get(index)).

    • testNextIndexAtTheBeginning

      public void testNextIndexAtTheBeginning()
      Test method to verify that nextIndex() returns 0 when the iterator is at the beginning of the list.

      Summary:

      This test verifies that the nextIndex() method correctly returns 0 when the HListIterator is positioned at the start of the list, before any elements have been traversed.

      Test Case Design:

      The test is designed to check the initial state of the iterator. This is a boundary condition test to ensure the iterator's cursor is correctly initialized and reports the first valid index (0) before any navigation.

      Test Description:

      Immediately after obtaining a new HListIterator from the vector, the test calls nextIndex() and asserts that the returned value is 0.

      Pre-Condition:

      - A VectorAdapter is initialized with elements: ["1", "2", "3", null, "5"]

      Test method to verify that set operation overrides previous set when called consecutively on same element.

      Summary:

      This test verifies that when set is called multiple times on the same element without intermediate operations, only the last set operation takes effect, overriding previous values.

      Test Case Design:

      The test is designed to validate the behavior of consecutive set operations on the same element, ensuring that the iterator correctly handles value replacement without creating duplicate or intermediate states.

      Test Description:

      The test advances the iterator, performs a set operation, moves back and performs another set operation on the same element, then verifies that only the last set value is present in the collection.

      Pre-Condition:

      - VectorAdapter initialized with ["1", "2", "3", null, "5"]

      - SubListAdapter created from indices 1 to 4

      - HListIterator positioned at beginning of sublist

      Post-Condition:

      - Second element of sublist contains the last set value "7"

      - Previous set value "6" is not present in the collection

      Expected Results:

      Consecutive set operations on the same element should result in only the last value being retained.

      Post-Condition:

      - No elements are accessible through the iterator

      Expected Results:

      hasNext() and hasPrevious() return false, nextIndex() returns 0, previousIndex() returns -1.

      Post-Condition:

      - Iterator correctly returns elements from starting index onward

      - Iterator reaches end of collection

      Expected Results:

      First next() returns "3", second next() returns null, hasNext() returns false after iteration.
